description: Clean energy and digital systems expand through mineral extraction and land-intensive infrastructure.
AI and digital platforms expand through data extraction cloud dependency predictive governance and hidden labor.
Wealthy states respond to climate stress through hardened borders resource control and security planning.
Dominant institutions dismiss reparative and decolonial futures as impractical or destabilizing.
Biodiversity and carbon projects expand through protected areas offsets and external ecological governance.
Development institutions promote modernization through infrastructure finance technology and market integration.
Communities youth workers Indigenous peoples migrants and civil society contest dominant scenarios and build alternatives.
Land finance climate policy technology and institutions are redesigned around repair and self-determination.
